questions.text: किसी पतली प्लास्टिक की छड़ को त्रिज्या R के वृत्ताकार वलय के रूप में मोड़ा गया है। इसे आवेश घनत्व λ से एकसमान आवेशित किया गया है। इसके केन्द्र पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र का परिमाण है :
questions.text_english: A thin plastic rod is bent into a circular ring of radius R. It is uniformly charged with charge density λ. The magnitude of the electric field at its centre is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Zero. For a uniformly charged circular ring, every small element of charge on the ring has an equal and opposite element diametrically across from it. By symmetry, the electric field contributions from all pairs of diametrically opposite elements cancel each other at the centre. Therefore, the net electric field at the centre of a uniformly charged ring is zero. Option A would apply if the field were due to an infinite line charge, option C is the Coulomb constant form which does not apply here, and option D has no standard derivation for this geometry.
questions.topic: Electric field due to a uniformly charged ring

questions.text: दस संधारित्र, जिनमें प्रत्येक की धारिता 1 μF है, को 100 V के स्रोत से पार्श्व में संयोजित किया गया है। इस निकाय में संचित कुल ऊर्जा है :
questions.text_english: Ten capacitors, each of capacitance 1 µF, are connected in parallel to a source of 100 V. The total energy stored in the system is equal to :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 5.0 × 10⁻² J. When capacitors are connected in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is C_eq = 10 × 1 μF = 10 μF = 10 × 10⁻⁶ F. The energy stored is U = ½C_eq V² = ½ × 10 × 10⁻⁶ × (100)² = ½ × 10 × 10⁻⁶ × 10000 = 5 × 10⁻² J. Options A, B, and C result from incorrect calculations of either the equivalent capacitance or the energy formula.
questions.topic: Energy stored in capacitors in parallel

questions.text: आरेख में दर्शाए गए परिपथ पर विचार कीजिए। इसके बिन्दु A और B के बीच विभवान्तर है :
questions.text_english: Consider the circuit shown in the figure. The potential difference between points A and B is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 9 V. Using Kirchhoff's laws: for the upper branch with EMF 12 V and resistance 1 Ω, and the lower branch with EMF 6 V and resistance 0.5 Ω, the current in the circuit can be determined. Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law and solving the two-mesh circuit, the potential difference between A and B works out to 9 V. Options 6 V and 12 V correspond to the individual EMFs, while 8 V results from an incorrect application of the superposition theorem.

questions.text: कोई पाश, जिससे धारा I दक्षिणावर्त प्रवाहित हो रही है, x – y तल में, z-अक्ष के अनुदिश किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में स्थित है। इस पाश की प्रवृत्ति होगी :
questions.text_english: A loop carrying a current I clockwise is placed in x – y plane, in a uniform magnetic field directed along z-axis. The tendency of the loop will be to :

options.A: x-अक्ष के अनुदिश गति करने की
options.B: y-अक्ष के अनुदिश गति करने की

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) shrink. A clockwise current loop in the x–y plane has its magnetic moment directed along the negative z-axis (by the right-hand rule). When placed in a uniform magnetic field along the z-axis, the loop experiences a torque that tries to align its magnetic moment with the field, but in a uniform field there is no net translational force. However, the magnetic force on each current-carrying side of the loop is directed radially inward (since the current flows clockwise and the field is along +z), causing the loop to tend to shrink. There is no tendency to translate along x or y in a uniform field, so options A and B are incorrect, and the loop shrinks rather than expands.
questions.topic: Force on a current loop in a uniform magnetic field

questions.text: कोई 10 cm लम्बा तार y-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है। इससे धनात्मक y-दिशा में 1.0 A की धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस क्षेत्र में कोई चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B = (5 mT)ĵ – (8 mT)k̂ विद्यमान है। इस तार पर बल है :
questions.text_english: A 10 cm long wire lies along y-axis. It carries a current of 1.0 A in positive y-direction. A magnetic field B = (5 mT)ĵ – (8 mT)k̂ exists in the region. The force on the wire is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (0.8 mN)î. The force on a current-carrying wire is F = I(L × B). Here, L = 0.10 ĵ m, I = 1.0 A, and B = (5 mT)ĵ – (8 mT)k̂. So F = 1.0 × [0.10 ĵ × (0.005 ĵ – 0.008 k̂)]. Since ĵ × ĵ = 0 and ĵ × k̂ = î, we get F = 1.0 × [0.10 × (–0.008) î] = –0.0008 × (–1) = wait, ĵ × (–k̂) = –(ĵ × k̂) = –î, so F = 1.0 × 0.10 × (–0.008)(–î) = 0.0008 î N = 0.8 mN î. The j-component contributes zero and only the k-component produces a force. The answer is +0.8 mN in the +î direction.
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field

questions.text: प्रतिरोध G के किसी गैल्वेनामीटर को 0 से I A परास के एमीटर में परिवर्तित किया गया है। यदि इस गैल्वेनोमीटर में प्रवाहित धारा I A की 0.1% है, तो एमीटर का प्रतिरोध है :
questions.text_english: A galvanometer of resistance G is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to I A. If the current through the galvanometer is 0.1% of I A, the resistance of the ammeter is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) G/999. The current through the galvanometer is Ig = 0.1% of I = I/1000. The shunt resistance S is given by Ig × G = (I – Ig) × S. So (I/1000) × G = (I – I/1000) × S = (999I/1000) × S, giving S = G/999. The ammeter resistance is the parallel combination: R_ammeter = GS/(G + S) = G(G/999)/(G + G/999) = (G²/999)/(1000G/999) = G/1000. However, the question asks for the resistance of the ammeter (the parallel combination of G and S), which equals G/1000. But if it asks for S (the shunt), S = G/999. Since the question says 'resistance of the ammeter' and the ammeter resistance = S·G/(S+G) = (G/999)·G/(G/999 + G) = G/1000. The correct answer for ammeter resistance is G/1000, option B. Re-examining: ammeter resistance = SG/(S+G) with S = G/999 gives G/1000, so the answer is (B) G/1000.

questions.text: आवृत्ति ω के किसी ac स्रोत से संयोजित धारिता C के किसी संधारित्र की प्रतिघात X है। यदि संधारित्र की धारिता को दो गुना और स्रोत की आवृत्ति को तीन गुना कर दिया जाए, तो प्रतिघात हो जाएगी :
questions.text_english: The reactance of a capacitor of capacitance C connected to an ac source of frequency ω is X. If the capacitance of the capacitor is doubled and the frequency of the source is tripled, the reactance will become :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) X/6. The capacitive reactance is X_C = 1/(ωC). Originally X = 1/(ωC). When capacitance is doubled (C' = 2C) and frequency is tripled (ω' = 3ω), the new reactance is X' = 1/(ω'C') = 1/(3ω × 2C) = 1/(6ωC) = X/6. Since both changes reduce the reactance (higher frequency and higher capacitance both lower X_C), the new value is one-sixth of the original. Option B (6X) would result if both changes increased reactance, which is incorrect.

questions.text: चार क्षेत्र I, II, III तथा IV में विद्युत-क्षेत्र निम्नलिखित रूप में वर्णित हैं: क्षेत्र I : Ex = E₀ sin(kz – ωt), क्षेत्र II : Ex = E₀, क्षेत्र III : Ex = E₀ sin kz, क्षेत्र IV : Ex = E₀ cos kz। किस क्षेत्र में विस्थापन धारा होगी ?
questions.text_english: In the four regions, I, II, III and IV, the electric fields are described as: Region I : Ex = E₀ sin(kz – ωt), Region II : Ex = E₀, Region III : Ex = E₀ sin kz, Region IV : Ex = E₀ cos kz. The displacement current will exist in the region :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Region I. Displacement current exists when the electric flux (and hence the electric field) changes with time. The displacement current density is J_d = ε₀(∂E/∂t). In Region I, Ex = E₀ sin(kz – ωt), which varies with time (it has a time-dependent term ωt), so ∂E/∂t ≠ 0, and displacement current exists. In Region II, Ex = E₀ is constant in time, so ∂E/∂t = 0. In Regions III and IV, the fields depend only on position z and not on time, so ∂E/∂t = 0. Only Region I has a time-varying electric field.

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के स्पेक्ट्रम में बामर श्रेणी की दूसरी स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखा के निर्माण में इलेक्ट्रॉन का जो संक्रमण होता है, वह संगत होता है :
questions.text_english: The transition of electron that gives rise to the formation of the second spectral line of the Balmer series in the spectrum of hydrogen atom corresponds to :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) nf = 2 and ni = 4. The Balmer series corresponds to transitions ending at n = 2 (nf = 2). The first line (Hα) involves the transition ni = 3 → nf = 2. The second line (Hβ) involves the transition ni = 4 → nf = 2. Therefore, the second spectral line of the Balmer series corresponds to nf = 2 and ni = 4. Option A gives the first Balmer line, option B is from the Paschen series (nf = 3), and option D gives the series limit (ionisation), not a specific line.

questions.text: Ge का मादन As के साथ किया गया है। इसके कारण :
questions.text_english: Ge is doped with As. Due to doping,

options.A: Ge के जालक की संरचना विकृत हो जाती है।
options.B: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.C: होलों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.D: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में कमी होती है।

options_english.A: the structure of Ge lattice is distorted.
options_english.B: the number of conduction electrons increases.
options_english.D: the number of conduction electrons decreases.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) the number of conduction electrons increases. Arsenic (As) is a pentavalent impurity (Group 15). When it replaces a germanium atom (tetravalent, Group 14) in the lattice, four of its five valence electrons form covalent bonds with neighbouring Ge atoms, and the fifth electron becomes a free conduction electron. This creates an n-type semiconductor with an increased number of free (conduction) electrons. The lattice structure is not significantly distorted (A is wrong), holes do not increase (C is wrong), and conduction electrons certainly do not decrease (D is wrong).

questions.text: दो पुञ्ज, A और B जिनके फ़ोटॉनों की ऊर्जा क्रमशः 3.3 eV और 11.3 eV हैं, क्रमवार किसी धात्विक पृष्ठ (कार्य-फलन 2.3 eV) को प्रदीप्त करते हैं। पुञ्ज A के कारण उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम चाल का पुञ्ज B की अधिकतम चाल से अनुपात है :
questions.text_english: Two beams, A and B whose photon energies are 3.3 eV and 11.3 eV respectively, illuminate a metallic surface (work function 2.3 eV) successively. The ratio of maximum speed of electrons emitted due to beam A to that due to beam B is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1/3. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is KE = hf – φ (work function). For beam A: KE_A = 3.3 – 2.3 = 1.0 eV. For beam B: KE_B = 11.3 – 2.3 = 9.0 eV. Since KE = ½mv², we have v ∝ √(KE). Therefore, v_A/v_B = √(KE_A/KE_B) = √(1.0/9.0) = √(1/9) = 1/3. The ratio of maximum speeds is 1/3.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: किसी गतिमान इलेक्ट्रॉन और किसी गतिमान प्रोटॉन से सम्बद्ध तरंगों का तरंगदैर्ध्य समान λ है। इसका यह अभिप्राय है कि इनका/इनकी समान है :
questions.text_english: The waves associated with a moving electron and a moving proton have the same wavelength λ. It implies that they have the same :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) momentum. According to de Broglie's relation, the wavelength λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is the momentum of the particle. If both the electron and the proton have the same de Broglie wavelength λ, then they must have the same momentum p = h/λ. They cannot have the same speed (C) because they have different masses, nor the same kinetic energy (D) since KE = p²/2m and the masses differ. Angular momentum (B) is a different quantity that is not directly determined by the de Broglie wavelength alone.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : प्रकाश-विद्युत प्रभाव में, उत्सर्जित फ़ोटोआपतित प्रकाश की तीव्रता में वृद्धि के साथ वृद्धि होती है।
कारण (R) : प्रकाश-विद्युत धारा आपतित प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य पर निर्भर करती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In photoelectric effect, the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons increases with increase in the intensity of the incident light.
Reason (R) : Photoelectric current depends on the wavelength of the incident light.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) वाले प्रश्न। सही उत्तर (A), (B), (C), (D) में से चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) type question. Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है तथा कारण (R) भी गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The Assertion is false: in the photoelectric effect, the kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons depends on the frequency (not the intensity) of the incident light. Increasing the intensity increases the number of emitted electrons (the photoelectric current) but does not increase the kinetic energy of individual electrons. The Reason is also false: the photoelectric current depends on the intensity of the incident light (not on the wavelength, as stated). The wavelength determines whether emission occurs at all and the maximum kinetic energy, but the current (number of electrons per unit time) depends on intensity.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जब दो कुण्डलियों को एक-दूसरे के ऊपर लपेटा जाता है, तो उनके बीच अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व अधिकतम होता है।
कारण (R) : जब दो कुण्डलियाँ एक-दूसरे के ऊपर लपेटी जाती हैं, तो उनके बीच फ्लक्स सम्बद्धता अधिकतम होती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The mutual inductance between two coils is maximum when the coils are wound on each other.
Reason (R) : The flux linkage between two coils is maximum when they are wound on each other.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है तथा कारण (R) भी गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Mutual inductance M is defined as the ratio of flux linkage in one coil due to the current in the other coil. When two coils are wound on each other (coaxially with the same geometry), virtually all the magnetic flux produced by one coil passes through the other, so the flux linkage is maximum. This maximum flux linkage directly leads to maximum mutual inductance. Therefore, both statements are correct and causally linked.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी बैटरी से श्रेणी में संयोजित और स्वतंत्रतापूर्वक निलम्बित दो लम्बे समान्तर तार एक-दूसरे से दूर हटते हैं।
कारण (R) : विपरीत दिशाओं में प्रवाहित धारावाही दो तार एक-दूसरे को प्रतिकर्षित करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Two long parallel wires, freely suspended and connected in series to a battery, move apart.
Reason (R) : Two wires carrying current in opposite directions repel each other.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है तथा कारण (R) भी गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. When two wires are connected in series to a battery, the current flows in one direction through one wire and returns through the other. This means the currents in the two wires flow in opposite directions. According to Ampere's law, two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions experience a repulsive force between them. Therefore, the freely suspended wires move apart, exactly as the Assertion states. The Reason (opposite currents repel) is the correct explanation for the Assertion (wires move apart).

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : समतल दर्पण और उत्तल दर्पण किसी भी परिस्थिति में वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब नहीं बना सकते हैं।
कारण (R) : कोई आभासी प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब बनाने के लिए बिम्ब की भाँति कार्य नहीं कर सकता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Plane and convex mirrors cannot produce real images under any circumstance.
Reason (R) : A virtual image cannot serve as an object to produce a real image.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है तथा कारण (R) भी गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is true: plane and convex mirrors always form virtual, erect images for real objects and cannot produce real images on their own. However, the Reason is false: a virtual image can indeed serve as a virtual object for another optical system (like a lens or another mirror) to produce a real image. For example, if converging light rays are intercepted by a plane mirror before they converge, the plane mirror can produce a real image by reflecting them. The Reason incorrectly states that virtual images cannot act as objects, which contradicts optical principles.

questions.text: वह ताप ज्ञात कीजिए जिस पर किसी सिल्वर से बने तार का प्रतिरोध उसके 20°C पर प्रतिरोध का दो गुना होगा। 20°C को संदर्भ ताप मान लीजिए और 20°C पर सिल्वर का प्रतिरोध का ताप गुणांक = 4.0 × 10⁻³ K⁻¹ लीजिए।
questions.text_english: Find the temperature at which the resistance of a wire made of silver will be twice its resistance at 20°C. Take 20°C as the reference temperature and temperature coefficient of resistance of silver at 20°C = 4.0 × 10⁻³ K⁻¹.

key_points: Use R = R₀[1 + α(T – T₀)]
Set R = 2R₀ and solve for T

questions.solution: Using the relation R(T) = R₀[1 + α(T – T₀)], where R₀ is resistance at T₀ = 20°C and α = 4.0 × 10⁻³ K⁻¹. Setting R(T) = 2R₀ gives 2R₀ = R₀[1 + α(T – 20)], so 1 = α(T – 20), giving T – 20 = 1/α = 1/(4.0 × 10⁻³) = 250 K. Therefore T = 20 + 250 = 270°C. The resistance of the silver wire will be twice its value at 20°C when the temperature reaches 270°C.

questions.text: (क) आवृत्ति 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz का एकवर्णी प्रकाश वायु से अपवर्तनांक 1.5 वाले माध्यम में गमन करता है। दोनों माध्यमों के अन्तरापृष्ठ पर (i) परावर्तित प्रकाश, तथा (ii) अपवर्तित प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Monochromatic light of frequency 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz passes from air into a medium of refractive index 1.5. Find the wavelength of the light (i) reflected, and (ii) refracted at the interface of the two media.
OR
(b) A plano-convex lens of focal length 16 cm is made of a material of refractive index 1.4. Calculate the radius of the curved surface of the lens.

key_points: For (a)(i): Reflected light remains in air; wavelength = c/f = 3×10⁸ / 5×10¹⁴ = 6×10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm
For (a)(ii): Refracted wavelength = λ_air / n = 600 nm / 1.5 = 400 nm
For (b): Using Lensmaker's equation 1/f = (n–1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂]; for plano-convex R₂ = ∞, so 1/f = (n–1)/R, giving R = (n–1)f = 0.4 × 16 = 6.4 cm

questions.solution:
Part (a): The frequency of light remains unchanged at any interface. (i) For reflected light (which stays in air): wavelength λ = c/f = (3 × 10⁸ m/s)/(5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz) = 6 × 10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm. (ii) For refracted light (which enters the medium of refractive index n = 1.5): the speed in the medium is v = c/n = 3×10⁸/1.5 = 2×10⁸ m/s. The wavelength in the medium is λ' = v/f = 2×10⁸/5×10¹⁴ = 4×10⁻⁷ m = 400 nm. Alternatively, λ' = λ/n = 600/1.5 = 400 nm.

Part (b): For a plano-convex lens, one surface is flat (R₂ = ∞) and one is convex (R₁ = R). Using the Lensmaker's equation: 1/f = (n – 1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂] = (1.4 – 1)[1/R – 0] = 0.4/R. Given f = 16 cm, R = 0.4 × 16 = 6.4 cm.

questions.text: कोई बिम्ब 40 cm वक्रता त्रिज्या के किसी अवतल दर्पण के सामने 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। (i) बने प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति तथा (ii) प्रतिबिम्ब का आवर्धन ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm. Find the (i) position of the image formed and (ii) magnification of the image.

key_points: Focal length f = –R/2 = –20 cm (concave mirror)
Object distance u = –30 cm (sign convention)
Magnification m = –v/u = –(–60)/(–30) = –2

questions.solution: Focal length of the concave mirror: f = –R/2 = –40/2 = –20 cm. Object distance u = –30 cm (real object). Using the mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, so 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = 1/(–20) – 1/(–30) = –1/20 + 1/30 = (–3 + 2)/60 = –1/60, giving v = –60 cm. The image is formed 60 cm in front of the mirror (real and inverted). Magnification m = –v/u = –(–60)/(–30) = –2. The image is real, inverted, and magnified by a factor of 2.

questions.text: गतिज ऊर्जा E के किसी न्यूट्रॉन (द्रव्यमान m) तथा समान ऊर्जा के किसी फ़ोटॉन पर विचार कीजिए। मान लीजिए न्यूट्रॉन की दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्ध्य λₙ तथा फ़ोटॉन की तरंगदैर्ध्य λₚ है। λₙ/λₚ के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Consider a neutron (mass m) of kinetic energy E and a photon of the same energy. Let λₙ and λₚ be the de Broglie wavelength of neutron and the wavelength of photon respectively. Obtain an expression for λₙ/λₚ.

key_points: For neutron: λₙ = h/p = h/√(2mE)
For photon: E = hc/λₚ, so λₚ = hc/E
Ratio: λₙ/λₚ = [h/√(2mE)] / [hc/E] = E/(c√(2mE)) = √(E/2mc²) or equivalently √(E)/(c√(2m))

questions.solution: For the neutron of kinetic energy E and mass m, the momentum is p = √(2mE). The de Broglie wavelength is λₙ = h/p = h/√(2mE). For the photon with the same energy E, using E = pc for a photon, the momentum is p_photon = E/c, so λₚ = h/p_photon = hc/E. The ratio λₙ/λₚ = [h/√(2mE)] ÷ [hc/E] = [h × E] / [hc × √(2mE)] = E / [c√(2mE)] = √(E) / [c√(2m)] = √(E/2mc²) / c × c = √(E/(2mc²)). Therefore, λₙ/λₚ = (1/c)√(E/2m).

questions.text: पदार्थ GaAs के लिए वोल्टता के साथ धारा के विचरण को दर्शाने वाला ग्राफ आरेखित कीजिए। इस ग्राफ पर वह क्षेत्र अंकित कीजिए जहाँ : (क) प्रतिरोध ऋणात्मक है, तथा (ख) ओम के नियम का पालन होता है।
questions.text_english: Plot a graph showing the variation of current with voltage for the material GaAs. On the graph, mark the region where : (a) resistance is negative, and (b) Ohm's law is obeyed.

key_points: GaAs has a non-linear I–V characteristic with a region of negative differential resistance
At low voltages (small V), I increases linearly — Ohm's law region
At a certain threshold voltage, I decreases with increasing V — negative resistance region
The graph shows a hump (peak) followed by a valley before current rises again

questions.solution: GaAs (Gallium Arsenide) exhibits a non-ohmic, non-linear I–V characteristic. At low applied voltages, the current increases linearly with voltage — this is the region where Ohm's law is obeyed, and the resistance is positive and constant. As the voltage increases beyond a threshold (around 3.1 V for bulk GaAs), a phenomenon called the Gunn effect occurs: electrons are transferred to a higher energy band with lower mobility, and the current actually decreases as voltage increases. This region of decreasing current with increasing voltage is the region of negative differential resistance. The graph thus shows a rising linear region (Ohm's law), a peak, a falling region (negative resistance), a valley, and then a rise again. The student should label the linear rising portion as 'Ohm's law region' and the falling portion (from peak to valley) as 'negative resistance region.'

questions.text: 0.1 m भुजा का कोई घन आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार उस प्रदेश में स्थित है जहाँ विद्युत-क्षेत्र E = 500 xî विद्यमान है। यहाँ x मीटर में तथा E, NC⁻¹ में है। परिकलित कीजिए : (क) घन से गुज़रने वाला फ्लक्स, तथा (ख) घन के भीतर आवेश।
questions.text_english: A cube of side 0.1 m is placed, as shown in the figure, in a region where electric field E = 500 xî exists. Here x is in meters and E in NC⁻¹. Calculate : (a) the flux passing through the cube, and (b) the charge within the cube.

key_points: Electric flux through left face (x = 0.1 m): Φ₁ = E₁ × A = 500×0.1 × (0.1)² = 50 × 0.01 = 0.5 N·m²/C (outward)
Electric flux through right face (x = 0.2 m): Φ₂ = 500×0.2 × (0.1)² = 100 × 0.01 = 1.0 N·m²/C (outward)
Net flux = Φ₂ – Φ₁ = 1.0 – 0.5 = 0.5 N·m²/C
Charge enclosed q = ε₀ × Φ_net = 8.854×10⁻¹² × 0.5 = 4.427×10⁻¹² C ≈ 4.43 pC

questions.solution: The electric field E = 500x î acts along the x-axis. Only the two faces perpendicular to the x-axis contribute to the net flux. Assuming the cube is placed from x = 0.1 m to x = 0.2 m (as indicated in the figure with 0.1 m marked). For the face at x = 0.1 m (left face, inward normal –î): E₁ = 500 × 0.1 = 50 N/C, flux Φ₁ = –50 × (0.1)² = –0.5 N·m²/C. For the face at x = 0.2 m (right face, outward normal +î): E₂ = 500 × 0.2 = 100 N/C, flux Φ₂ = +100 × (0.1)² = +1.0 N·m²/C. Net flux Φ = Φ₁ + Φ₂ = –0.5 + 1.0 = 0.5 N·m²/C. By Gauss's law, the charge enclosed is q = ε₀Φ = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² × 0.5 ≈ 4.43 × 10⁻¹² C = 4.43 pC.

questions.text: (क) 'धारा घनत्व' को परिभाषित कीजिए। क्या यह अदिश है या सदिश ? किसी धातु के चालक में कोई विद्युत-क्षेत्र E बनाए रखा गया है। यदि इस चालक के प्रति एकांक आयतन में इलेक्ट्रॉनों (द्रव्यमान m, आवेश –e) की संख्या n है तथा इसका विश्रान्ति काल τ है, तो यह दर्शाइए कि धारा घनत्व j = αE है, जहाँ α = (ne²/m)τ है।
questions.text_english:
(a) Define 'current density'. Is it a scalar or a vector? An electric field E is maintained in a metallic conductor. If n be the number of electrons (mass m, charge –e) per unit volume in the conductor and τ its relaxation time, show that the current density j = αE, where α = (ne²/m)τ.
OR
(b) What is a Wheatstone bridge? Obtain the necessary conditions under which the Wheatstone bridge is balanced.

key_points: Current density j = current per unit area perpendicular to flow; it is a vector quantity
Drift velocity: vd = eEτ/m (from Newton's second law and relaxation time model)
Current density: j = nevd = n × e × (eEτ/m) = (ne²τ/m)E = αE where α = ne²τ/m
For Wheatstone bridge: four resistors P, Q, R, S in a bridge; balanced when P/Q = R/S (no current through galvanometer)

questions.solution:
Part (a): Current density is defined as the amount of current flowing per unit cross-sectional area perpendicular to the direction of current flow. It is a vector quantity, directed along the direction of current (opposite to electron flow). In a metallic conductor with electric field E, the force on each electron is F = eE (magnitude). By Newton's second law, acceleration a = eE/m. The drift velocity is vd = aτ = eEτ/m. The current density is j = n(–e)(–vd) = nevd = ne(eEτ/m) = (ne²τ/m)E = αE, where α = ne²τ/m. This proves the relation j = αE.

Part (b): A Wheatstone bridge is an electrical circuit used to measure unknown resistance accurately. It consists of four resistors P, Q, R, and S arranged in a diamond (bridge) configuration, with a battery across one diagonal and a galvanometer across the other. The bridge is balanced when no current flows through the galvanometer. This condition requires P/Q = R/S, or equivalently PS = QR. At balance, the potential at the two middle nodes is equal, so no current flows through the galvanometer branch.

questions.text: 1.3384 × 10⁻¹⁴ J गतिज ऊर्जा का कोई प्रोटॉन, पूर्व दिशा के अनुदिश दिशिक 2.0 mT के किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B में, उत्तर से दक्षिण की ओर क्षैतिजत: गतिमान होते हुए प्रवेश करता है। परिकलित कीजिए : (क) प्रोटॉन की चाल, (ख) प्रोटॉन में उत्पन्न त्वरण का परिमाण, (ग) प्रोटॉन के गमन पथ की त्रिज्या।
questions.text_english: A proton with kinetic energy 1.3384 × 10⁻¹⁴ J moving horizontally from north to south, enters a uniform magnetic field B of 2.0 mT directed eastward. Calculate : (a) the speed of the proton, (b) the magnitude of acceleration of the proton, (c) the radius of the path traced by the proton. [Take (q/m) for proton = 1.0 × 10⁸ C/kg]

key_points: Mass of proton m = 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg; q/m = 1.0 × 10⁸ C/kg
Acceleration: a = qvB/m = (q/m)vB = 10⁸ × 4×10⁶ × 2×10⁻³ = 8 × 10¹¹ m/s²

questions.solution:
Given: KE = 1.3384 × 10⁻¹⁴ J, B = 2.0 mT = 2.0 × 10⁻³ T, q/m = 1.0 × 10⁸ C/kg. Mass of proton m = 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.

(a) Speed: KE = ½mv², so v = √(2KE/m) = √(2 × 1.3384 × 10⁻¹⁴ / 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷) = √(1.6 × 10¹³) = 4 × 10⁶ m/s.

(b) The magnetic force provides centripetal acceleration: F = qvB, so a = F/m = (q/m)vB = 1.0 × 10⁸ × 4 × 10⁶ × 2.0 × 10⁻³ = 8.0 × 10¹¹ m/s².

(c) Radius of circular path: r = mv/(qB) = v/(q/m × B) = (4 × 10⁶)/(1.0 × 10⁸ × 2.0 × 10⁻³) = (4 × 10⁶)/(2 × 10⁵) = 20 m.

questions.text: कोई प्रेरक, कोई संधारित्र और कोई प्रतिरोधक किसी ac स्रोत v = vₘ sin ωt से श्रेणी में संयोजित हैं। परिपथ में क्षयित औसत शक्ति के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए। परिपथ की अनुनाद आवृत्ति के लिए भी व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An inductor, a capacitor and a resistor are connected in series with an ac source v = vₘ sin ωt. Derive an expression for the average power dissipated in the circuit. Also obtain the expression for the resonant frequency of the circuit.

key_points: Instantaneous power P = vi; current i = iₘ sin(ωt – φ)
Average power P_avg = ½ vₘiₘ cos φ = V_rms × I_rms × cos φ (power factor cos φ = R/Z)
P_avg = V²_rms R / Z² = I²_rms R
Resonant frequency: at resonance X_L = X_C, ωL = 1/(ωC), ω₀ = 1/√(LC), f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC))

questions.solution:
In an LCR series circuit with ac source v = vₘ sin ωt, the current is i = iₘ sin(ωt – φ), where iₘ = vₘ/Z, Z = √[R² + (X_L – X_C)²] is the impedance, and φ is the phase angle with cos φ = R/Z. The instantaneous power is P = v × i = vₘ sin ωt × iₘ sin(ωt – φ). Expanding and averaging over a complete cycle, the terms with sin 2ωt and cos 2ωt average to zero, giving average power P_avg = ½ vₘiₘ cos φ = V_rms × I_rms × cos φ, where V_rms = vₘ/√2 and I_rms = iₘ/√2. This can be written as P_avg = I²_rms × R, showing that power is dissipated only in the resistor.

For resonant frequency: at resonance, the impedance is minimum and purely resistive. This occurs when X_L = X_C, i.e., ωL = 1/(ωC). Solving, ω₀ = 1/√(LC) rad/s, or f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)) Hz.

(क) विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग की तरंगदैर्ध्य को प्रायः विकिरण उत्पन्न करने वाले निकाय के अभिलाक्षणिक साइज़ से संबंधित किया जाता है। इस कथन की पुष्टि के लिए दो उदाहरण दीजिए।
(ख) (i) लम्बी दूरियों के रेडियो प्रसारण के लिए लघु-तरंग बैण्ड का उपयोग किया जाता है। क्यों?
(ii) प्रकाशिक और रेडियो दूरबीन (दूरदर्शक) धरती पर स्थापित की जाती हैं, परन्तु X-किरण खगोलिकी केवल पृथ्वी की कक्षा में परिक्रमा करने वाले उपग्रहों से ही संभव है। क्यों ?
questions.text_english:
(a) The wavelength of an electromagnetic wave is generally associated with the characteristic size of the system that emits it. Give two examples to justify this statement.
(b) (i) Long distance radio broadcasts use short-wave bands. Why?
(ii) Optical and radio telescopes are built on the ground, but X-ray astronomy is possible only from satellites orbiting the Earth. Why?

key_points: Example 1: Nuclear transitions (nucleus ~10⁻¹⁵ m) emit gamma rays (λ ~10⁻¹² m)
Example 2: Atomic electron transitions (~10⁻¹⁰ m) emit visible/UV light (λ ~10⁻⁷ m)
Short-wave (HF) bands are reflected by the ionosphere, enabling long-distance radio propagation
X-rays are absorbed by the Earth's atmosphere; satellites above the atmosphere can detect them

questions.solution:
Part (a): Two examples justifying the connection between wavelength and source size: (1) Atoms have a characteristic size of about 10⁻¹⁰ m. Transitions of electrons in atoms emit visible or ultraviolet light with wavelengths around 10⁻⁷ m, which is of the same order as the atomic size. (2) Atomic nuclei have a characteristic size of about 10⁻¹⁵ m. Nuclear transitions emit gamma rays with wavelengths around 10⁻¹² m, which is comparable to the nuclear dimensions. Radio antennas of size ~1 m emit radio waves of wavelength ~1 m, further illustrating the principle.

Part (b)(i): Short-wave bands (high frequency, 3–30 MHz) are reflected by the ionosphere back to the Earth's surface, allowing the signal to travel long distances by multiple reflections between the ionosphere and the ground. Medium and long waves are absorbed or less efficiently reflected.

(ii): The Earth's atmosphere is opaque to X-rays, absorbing them before they reach the ground. Optical telescopes work because the atmosphere is transparent to visible light. Radio telescopes work because the atmosphere transmits radio waves. However, X-rays can only be detected above the atmosphere, so X-ray astronomy requires satellites orbiting in space.

questions.text: रदरफोर्ड के परमाणु मॉडल की कमियाँ लिखिए। बोर ने उन्हें किस प्रकार दूर किया ? यह दर्शाइए कि बोर परमाणु की विभिन्न कक्षाओं के बीच की दूरियाँ समान नहीं होतीं हैं।
questions.text_english: Write the drawbacks of Rutherford's atomic model. How did Bohr overcome them? Show that the distances between different orbits of the Bohr atom are not equal.

key_points: Drawbacks: (1) Classical EM theory predicts accelerating electron should radiate and spiral into nucleus; (2) Cannot explain discrete line spectra of hydrogen
Bohr's postulates: electrons orbit in stationary states where angular momentum = nℏ; radiation emitted/absorbed only during transitions
Radius of nth orbit: rₙ = n²a₀ where a₀ = 0.529 Å; hence r₁=a₀, r₂=4a₀, r₃=9a₀
Differences: r₂–r₁ = 3a₀, r₃–r₂ = 5a₀, r₄–r₃ = 7a₀ — not equal, showing orbits are not equally spaced

questions.solution:
Rutherford's atomic model had two major drawbacks: (1) According to classical electromagnetic theory, an electron moving in a circular orbit is continuously accelerating and must continuously radiate energy. This would cause the electron to lose energy and spiral inward, ultimately collapsing into the nucleus within about 10⁻⁸ s. This contradicted the observed stability of atoms. (2) The model could not explain the discrete line spectrum of hydrogen or any other element.

Bohr overcame these limitations by proposing two postulates: (1) Electrons revolve in certain discrete, stationary orbits without radiating energy. These are orbits where the angular momentum is an integral multiple of ℏ: L = nℏ. (2) Radiation is emitted or absorbed only when an electron transitions from one allowed orbit to another, with energy hf = E₂ – E₁.

The radius of the nth Bohr orbit is rₙ = n²a₀, where a₀ = 0.529 Å (Bohr radius). So r₁ = a₀, r₂ = 4a₀, r₃ = 9a₀, r₄ = 16a₀. The gaps between successive orbits are: r₂ – r₁ = 3a₀, r₃ – r₂ = 5a₀, r₄ – r₃ = 7a₀. Since these differences (3a₀, 5a₀, 7a₀, ...) are unequal, the orbits are not uniformly spaced.

questions.text:
(क) नाभिक के किन्हीं दो गुणों को लिखिए।
(ख) किसी नाभिक का घनत्व किसी परमाणु के घनत्व से बहुत अधिक क्यों है ?
(ग) यह दर्शाइए कि सभी नाभिकों के लिए नाभिकीय द्रव्य का घनत्व समान होता है।
questions.text_english:
(a) State any two properties of a nucleus.
(b) Why is the density of a nucleus much more than that of an atom?
(c) Show that the density of the nuclear matter is the same for all nuclei.

key_points: Two properties: (1) Nucleus has positive charge equal to Ze; (2) Nuclear size follows R = R₀A^(1/3) where R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm
Nucleus is very small (~10⁻¹⁵ m) compared to atom (~10⁻¹⁰ m) but contains almost all the mass, hence very high density
Nuclear density: ρ = (mass)/(volume) = (A × mₙ) / (4/3 π R³) = (A × mₙ) / (4/3 π R₀³A) = 3mₙ/(4πR₀³) — independent of A

questions.solution:
Part (a): Two properties of a nucleus: (1) The nucleus carries a positive charge of magnitude Ze, where Z is the atomic number and e is the elementary charge. (2) The size (radius) of a nucleus follows the empirical relation R = R₀A^(1/3), where A is the mass number and R₀ ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m (1.2 fm). This means the volume is proportional to A.

Part (b): The mass of an atom is concentrated almost entirely in its nucleus (protons and neutrons), while electrons contribute negligible mass. The nucleus has a radius of about 10⁻¹⁵ m, while the atom has a radius of about 10⁻¹⁰ m — a factor of 10⁵ difference. Since density = mass/volume and volume ∝ r³, the nucleus is about 10¹⁵ times denser than the atom.

Part (c): The mass of a nucleus of mass number A is approximately A × mₙ (mₙ = mass of nucleon). The volume of the nucleus is (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π(R₀A^(1/3))³ = (4/3)πR₀³A. Therefore, the nuclear density ρ = (A × mₙ)/[(4/3)πR₀³A] = 3mₙ/(4πR₀³). Since A cancels, ρ is independent of A and the same for all nuclei.

questions.text: कोई लेंस दो पृष्ठों से घिरा कोई पारदर्शी माध्यम होता है जिसका एक अथवा दोनों पृष्ठ गोलीय होते हैं। किसी लेंस की फोकस दूरी उसके दोनों पृष्ठों की वक्रता त्रिज्याओं और लेंस के पदार्थ के, उस पदार्थ के सापेक्ष जिससे लेंस घिरा है, अपवर्तनांक द्वारा निर्धारित की जाती है। किसी लेंस की क्षमता उसकी फोकस दूरी की व्युत्क्रम होती है। यदि कई लेंसों को सम्पर्क में रखा जाता है, तो संयोजन की क्षमता उन लेंसों की अपनी-अपनी क्षमताओं का बीजगणितीय योग होता है।
questions.text_english: A lens is a transparent medium bounded by two surfaces, with one or both surfaces being spherical. The focal length of a lens is determined by the radii of curvature of its two surfaces and the refractive index of its medium with respect to that of the surrounding medium. The power of a lens is reciprocal of its focal length. If a number of lenses are kept in contact, the power of the combination is the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses.

sub_questions.text: किसी काँच के बने उभयोत्तल लेंस के दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या R समान है तथा काँच का अपवर्तनांक n है। इस लेंस की क्षमता है :
sub_questions.text_english: A double-convex lens, with each face having same radius of curvature R, is made of glass of refractive index n. Its power is :
sub_questions.solution: For a double-convex lens with both radii of curvature equal to R (R₁ = +R, R₂ = –R by sign convention), the Lensmaker's equation gives 1/f = (n–1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂] = (n–1)[1/R – (–1/R)] = (n–1)(2/R) = 2(n–1)/R. Power P = 1/f = 2(n–1)/R.

sub_questions.text: क्षमता P के किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस, जिसके दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या समान है, को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के लम्बवत् दो समान भागों में काटा गया है। लेंस के एक भाग की क्षमता होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: A double-convex lens of power P, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to its principal axis. The power of one part of the lens will be :
sub_questions.solution: When a double-convex lens is cut perpendicular to the principal axis (i.e., horizontally), each half still has one curved surface (radius R) and one flat surface. The flat surface has R = ∞. Using the Lensmaker's equation for each half: 1/f' = (n–1)[1/R – 1/∞] = (n–1)/R. But the original lens had 1/f = 2(n–1)/R = P. So 1/f' = (n–1)/R = P/2, giving P' = P/2... However, reconsidering: when cut perpendicular to the principal axis (i.e., a horizontal cut creating a top and bottom half), the geometry and optical path are unchanged for paraxial rays. Each half acts as a plano-convex lens with f' = R/(n–1). Since f = R/(2(n–1)) = 1/P, we get f' = 2f, so P' = P/2. The answer is (D) P/2. Wait — the original lens has P = 2(n–1)/R, so each half (plano-convex) has P' = (n–1)/R = P/2. The correct answer is (D) P/2.

sub_questions.text: उपर्युक्त लेंस के दोनों भागों को आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार एक-दूसरे के सम्पर्क में रखा गया है। इस संयोजन की क्षमता होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The above two parts are kept in contact with each other as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be :
sub_questions.solution: When the two halves (each of power P/2) are placed in contact as shown (flat faces together, resembling the original lens), the combined power is P_total = P' + P' = P/2 + P/2 = P. The combination behaves like the original lens and has power P.

(a) A double-convex lens of power P, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut along its principal axis. The two parts are arranged as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be :
OR
(b) Two convex lenses of focal lengths 60 cm and 20 cm are held coaxially in contact with each other. The power of the combination is :

If the two halves are placed as shown (with the curved sides facing outward and flat sides adjacent, but offset or mirrored), the powers of the two halves cancel each other (+P/2 and –P/2 if one is inverted) or the combination is such that the net power is P/2 + P/2 = P. But if the cut is along the principal axis (vertical cut), each half is still a plano-convex lens of power P/2. When placed as shown in the figure (with curved faces both on same side), P_total = P. questions.text: संधि डायोड दिष्टकारी के रूप में: ac वोल्टता को दिष्ट (dc) वोल्टता में परिवर्तित करने की प्रक्रिया को दिष्टकरण कहते हैं और इस परिवर्तन को सम्पन्न करने वाली युक्ति को दिष्टकारी कहते हैं। किसी p-n संधि डायोड के अभिलाक्षणिक से यह ज्ञात होता है कि जब p-n संधि डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध निम्न होता है तथा जब पश्चदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध उच्च होता है। p-n संधि डायोड केवल अग्रदिशिक बायस होने पर ही चालन करता है।
questions.text_english: Junction Diode as a Rectifier: The process of conversion of an ac voltage into a dc voltage is called rectification and the device which performs this conversion is called a rectifier. The characteristics of a p-n junction diode reveal that when a p-n junction diode is forward biased, it offers a low resistance and when it is reverse biased, it offers a high resistance. Hence, a p-n junction diode conducts only when it is forward biased. This property of a p-n junction diode makes it suitable for its use as a rectifier. Thus, when an ac voltage is applied across a p-n junction, it conducts only during those alternate half cycles for which it is forward biased. A rectifier which rectifies only half cycle of an ac voltage is called a half-wave rectifier and one that rectifies both the half cycles is known as a full-wave rectifier.

sub_questions.text: किसी पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी पर अनुप्रयुक्त किसी प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता का वर्ग माध्य मूल मान V₀/√2 है। तो दिष्टीकृत निर्गत वोल्टता का वर्ग माध्य मूल मान है :
sub_questions.text_english: The root mean square value of an alternating voltage applied to a full-wave rectifier is V₀/√2. Then the root mean square value of the rectified output voltage is :
sub_questions.solution: The rms value of the input ac voltage is V_rms = V₀/√2, which means the peak voltage is V₀. A full-wave rectifier rectifies both half-cycles, so the output has the same peak value V₀. The rms value of a full-wave rectified sinusoid is the same as the rms value of the original sinusoid = V₀/√2. Therefore, the rms of the rectified output is V₀/√2.

sub_questions.text: किसी पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी में प्रत्येक डायोड से धारा प्रवाहित होती है :
sub_questions.text_english: In a full-wave rectifier, the current in each of the diodes flows for :

options.A: निवेश सिग्नल के पूर्ण चक्र के लिए
options.B: निवेश सिग्नल के अर्ध-चक्र के लिए
options.C: निवेश सिग्नल के अर्ध-चक्र से कम के लिए
options.D: निवेश सिग्नल के केवल धनात्मक अर्ध-चक्र के लिए

options_english.A: Complete cycle of the input signal
options_english.B: Half cycle of the input signal
options_english.C: Less than half cycle of the input signal
options_english.D: Only for the positive half cycle of the input signal

sub_questions.solution: In a full-wave rectifier (using two diodes and a centre-tap transformer, or a bridge rectifier with four diodes), each diode conducts for only one half-cycle of the input signal. In the positive half-cycle, one diode is forward biased and conducts; in the negative half-cycle, the other diode (or pair) conducts. So each individual diode carries current for half a cycle.

options.A: किसी निश्चित समय पर दोनों डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।
options.B: किसी निश्चित समय पर दोनों डायोड पश्चदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।
options.C: किसी निश्चित समय पर एक अग्रदिशिक बायसित तथा दूसरा पश्चदिशिक बायसित होता है।
options.D: प्रथम अर्ध-चक्र में दोनों अग्रदिशिक बायसित होते हैं तथा द्वितीय अर्ध-चक्र में पश्चदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।

options_english.A: Both diodes are forward biased at the same time.
options_english.B: Both diodes are reverse biased at the same time.
options_english.C: One is forward biased and the other is reverse biased at the same time.
options_english.D: Both are forward biased in the first half of the cycle and reverse biased in the second half of the cycle.

sub_questions.solution: In a full-wave rectifier, at any given instant during the ac cycle, one diode is forward biased (conducting) and the other is reverse biased (not conducting). This alternating conduction ensures that both half-cycles of the input are converted into a unidirectional output. At no instant are both diodes simultaneously forward biased or simultaneously reverse biased.

(ख) आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार कोई सिग्नल किसी p-n संधि डायोड पर अनुप्रयुक्त किया गया है। प्रतिरोध R_L के सिरों पर निर्गत की पहचान कीजिए :
sub_questions.text_english:
(a) An alternating voltage of frequency of 50 Hz is applied to a half-wave rectifier. Then the ripple frequency of the output will be :
OR
(b) A signal, as shown in the figure, is applied to a p-n junction diode. Identify the output across resistance R_L :

options_english.A: 100 Hz (for part a) / Output (A) as shown in figure (for part b)
options_english.B: 50 Hz (for part a) / Output (B) as shown in figure (for part b)
options_english.C: 25 Hz (for part a) / Output (C) as shown in figure (for part b)
options_english.D: 150 Hz (for part a) / Output (D) as shown in figure (for part b)

sub_questions.solution:
Part (a): For a half-wave rectifier, only one half-cycle of the input is passed to the output. If the input frequency is 50 Hz, the output has one pulse per full input cycle, so the ripple frequency equals the input frequency = 50 Hz. (For a full-wave rectifier it would be 100 Hz, but for half-wave it remains 50 Hz.) Answer: (B) 50 Hz.

Part (b): The signal alternates between +5 V and –5 V. The p-n junction diode conducts only during forward bias (positive half, i.e., +5 V portions). During the negative portion (–5 V), the diode is reverse biased and no current flows through R_L. Therefore, the output across R_L shows only the positive +5 V pulses with zero during the negative portions. This corresponds to option (D), which shows a positive half-wave rectified output at +5 V.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Derive an expression for potential energy of an electric dipole p in an external uniform electric field E. When is the potential energy of the dipole (1) maximum, and (2) minimum?
(ii) An electric dipole consists of point charges –1.0 pC and +1.0 pC located at (0,0) and (3 mm, 4 mm) respectively in x–y plane. An electric field E = 1000 V/m î is switched on in the region. Find the torque acting on the dipole.
OR
(b) (i) An electric dipole (dipole moment p = p î), consisting of charges –q and +q, separated by distance 2a, is placed along the x-axis, with its centre at the origin. Show that the potential V, due to this dipole, at a point x (x >> a) is equal to (1/4πε₀)·(p/x²).
(ii) Two isolated metallic spheres S₁ and S₂ of radii 1 cm and 3 cm respectively are charged such that both have the same charge density 10⁻⁹ C/m². They are placed far away from each other and connected by a thin wire. Calculate the new charge on sphere S₁.

key_points: Potential energy U = –pE cosθ = –p·E
U maximum (= +pE) when θ = 180° (dipole antiparallel to E)
U minimum (= –pE) when θ = 0° (dipole parallel to E)
Dipole moment: separation = √(3²+4²) mm = 5 mm = 5×10⁻³ m; p = q×d = 1×10⁻¹²×5×10⁻³ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ C·m
Torque τ = p × E; |τ| = pE sinθ where θ is angle between p and E

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): Consider an electric dipole of moment p making an angle θ with a uniform electric field E. The torque on the dipole is τ = pE sinθ (tends to align p with E). The potential energy is obtained by integrating work done against the torque: U = –∫τ dθ = –∫pE sinθ dθ = pE cosθ + C. Taking U = 0 at θ = 90°, we get U = –pE cosθ = –p·E. (1) U is maximum (= +pE) when θ = 180°, i.e., the dipole is antiparallel to the field — this is the position of unstable equilibrium. (2) U is minimum (= –pE) when θ = 0°, i.e., the dipole is parallel to the field — this is the position of stable equilibrium.

Part (a)(ii): The separation between the charges is d = √((3×10⁻³)² + (4×10⁻³)²) = √(9+16)×10⁻³ = 5×10⁻³ m. Dipole moment p = q × d = 1.0×10⁻¹² × 5×10⁻³ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ C·m. The dipole vector p points from –q to +q, i.e., from (0,0) to (3 mm, 4 mm). The unit vector is (3î + 4ĵ)/5. So p = 5×10⁻¹⁵ × (3î + 4ĵ)/5 = (3î + 4ĵ)×10⁻¹⁵ C·m. The torque τ = p × E = (3î + 4ĵ)×10⁻¹⁵ × 1000î = 10⁻¹²[(3î × î) + (4ĵ × î)] = 10⁻¹²[0 + 4(–k̂)] = –4×10⁻¹² k̂ N·m. The magnitude of torque is 4×10⁻¹² N·m.

Part (b)(i): The potential at point x on the x-axis from a dipole with +q at x = +a and –q at x = –a is V = (q/4πε₀)[1/(x–a) – 1/(x+a)] = (q/4πε₀)[2a/(x²–a²)]. For x >> a, x²–a² ≈ x², so V ≈ (q·2a)/(4πε₀x²) = p/(4πε₀x²) = (1/4πε₀)(p/x²).

Part (b)(ii): Initial charge on S₁: Q₁ = σ × 4πr₁² = 10⁻⁹ × 4π × (0.01)² = 4π×10⁻¹³ C. Initial charge on S₂: Q₂ = 10⁻⁹ × 4π × (0.03)² = 4π×9×10⁻¹³ C = 36π×10⁻¹³ C. Total charge: Q = Q₁+Q₂ = 4π×10⁻¹³(1+9) = 40π×10⁻¹³ C. After connecting, the potential equalises: V₁ = V₂, so Q₁'/r₁ = Q₂'/r₂, giving Q₁'/0.01 = Q₂'/0.03, so Q₂' = 3Q₁'. With Q₁' + Q₂' = Q: Q₁' + 3Q₁' = 40π×10⁻¹³, 4Q₁' = 40π×10⁻¹³, Q₁' = 10π×10⁻¹³ ≈ 3.14×10⁻¹² C.

(क) (i) किसी ac स्रोत v = vₘ sin ωt से किसी प्रतिरोधक और किसी संधारित्र को श्रेणी में संयोजित किया गया है। परिपथ की प्रतिबाधा के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए।

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series to an ac source v = vₘ sin ωt. Derive an expression for the impedance of the circuit.
(ii) When does an inductor act as a conductor in a circuit? Give reason for it.
(iii) An electric lamp is designed to operate at 110 V dc and 11 A current. If the lamp is operated on 220 V, 50 Hz ac source with a coil in series, then find the inductance of the coil.
OR
(b) (i) Draw a labelled diagram of a step-up transformer and describe its working principle. Explain any three causes for energy losses in a real transformer.
(ii) A step-up transformer converts a low voltage into high voltage. Does it violate the principle of conservation of energy? Explain.
(iii) A step-up transformer has 200 and 3000 turns in its primary and secondary coils respectively. The input voltage given to the primary coil is 90 V. Calculate: (1) The output voltage across the secondary coil, (2) The current in the primary coil if the current in the secondary coil is 2.0 A.

key_points: Impedance of RC circuit: Z = √(R² + X_C²) = √(R² + 1/(ωC)²)
Inductor acts as conductor at very high frequencies (X_L = ωL → ∞ means it blocks; at dc/very low frequency X_L → 0, acts as conductor)
Lamp resistance R = V/I = 110/11 = 10 Ω; in series with inductor on 220 V ac; current must remain 11 A; Z = 220/11 = 20 Ω; X_L = √(Z²–R²) = √(400–100) = √300 Ω; L = X_L/(2πf) = √300/(100π) H
For transformer: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p; output = 90×3000/200 = 1350 V; I_p = I_s × N_s/N_p = 2×3000/200 = 30 A

Part (a)(i): In a series RC circuit with ac source v = vₘ sinωt, the voltage across R is V_R = IR (in phase with current) and across C is V_C = IX_C = I/(ωC) (lagging current by 90°). By phasor analysis, the total voltage phasor has magnitude V = √(V_R² + V_C²) = I√(R² + X_C²). The impedance is Z = V/I = √(R² + X_C²) = √(R² + (1/ωC)²). The phase angle φ = arctan(X_C/R).

Part (a)(ii): An inductor acts as a conductor (offers negligible resistance) when the frequency of the ac source is very low or when dc is applied. The inductive reactance X_L = ωL = 2πfL. At very low frequencies (f → 0) or for dc (f = 0), X_L → 0, so the inductor behaves like a pure conductor (a short circuit). At dc, there is no change in flux, hence no back-EMF, and only the small ohmic resistance of the coil wire opposes the current.

Part (a)(iii): The lamp's resistance R = V/I = 110/11 = 10 Ω. On 220 V ac, the current must still be 11 A for the lamp to operate normally. The required impedance Z = V_rms/I = 220/11 = 20 Ω. Since Z = √(R² + X_L²), we get X_L = √(Z² – R²) = √(400 – 100) = √300 = 10√3 Ω. The inductance L = X_L/(2πf) = 10√3/(2π×50) = 10√3/(100π) ≈ 0.055 H ≈ 55 mH.

Part (b)(i): A step-up transformer has more turns in the secondary coil than in the primary. Working principle: An alternating current in the primary coil creates a changing magnetic flux in the iron core, which induces an EMF in the secondary coil (mutual induction). The ratio of output to input voltage equals the turns ratio N_s/N_p > 1 for step-up. Three causes of energy losses: (1) Joule heating (copper losses) due to resistance of coil wires; (2) Eddy current losses in the iron core (minimised by using laminated cores); (3) Hysteresis losses due to repeated magnetisation and demagnetisation of the core material.

Part (b)(ii): A step-up transformer increases voltage but does not violate conservation of energy. It increases voltage while decreasing current proportionally, so the power (V×I) remains constant (ideally). Since P_input = P_output in an ideal transformer, energy is conserved. The transformer merely transfers energy from primary to secondary through the changing magnetic field — it does not create energy.

Part (b)(iii): (1) Output voltage: V_s = V_p × N_s/N_p = 90 × 3000/200 = 90 × 15 = 1350 V. (2) Primary current: In an ideal transformer, P_p = P_s, so V_p × I_p = V_s × I_s, giving I_p = V_s × I_s/V_p = 1350 × 2.0/90 = 30 A. Alternatively, I_p/I_s = N_s/N_p, so I_p = 2.0 × 3000/200 = 30 A.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A ray of light passes through a triangular prism. Show graphically, how the angle of deviation varies with the angle of incidence? Hence define the angle of minimum deviation.
(ii) A ray of light is incident normally on a refracting face of a prism of prism angle A and suffers a deviation of angle δ. Prove that the refractive index n of the material of the prism is given by n = sin(A+δ)/sinA.
(iii) The refractive index of the material of a prism is √2. If the refracting angle of the prism is 60°, find the (1) Angle of minimum deviation, and (2) Angle of incidence.
OR
(b) (i) State Huygens' principle. A plane wave is incident at an angle i on a reflecting surface. Construct the corresponding reflected wavefront. Using this diagram, prove that the angle of reflection is equal to the angle of incidence.
(ii) What are the coherent sources of light? Can two independent sodium lamps act like coherent sources? Explain.
(iii) A beam of light consisting of a known wavelength 520 nm and an unknown wavelength λ in Young's double-slit experiment produces two interference patterns such that the fourth bright fringe of unknown wavelength coincides with the fifth bright fringe of known wavelength. Find the value of λ.

key_points: Graph: δ vs i is a U-shaped curve with minimum at i = i_min; angle of minimum deviation δ_m defined at the bottom of the curve
For normal incidence on one face: r₁ = 0, r₂ = A; using Snell's law at second face: n sin A = sin(A+δ); hence n = sin(A+δ)/sinA
Angle of incidence at min deviation: i = (A+δ_m)/2 = (60°+30°)/2 = 45°
Huygens' principle: every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets; law of reflection proof using wavefront geometry
Coherent sources have constant phase difference; two independent Na lamps cannot be coherent due to random phase changes

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): When a ray of light passes through a triangular prism, the total angle of deviation δ depends on the angle of incidence i. A graph of δ versus i is a U-shaped (hyperbolic) curve. As i increases from the critical minimum value, δ first decreases, reaches a minimum value δ_m, and then increases again. The angle of minimum deviation δ_m is defined as the smallest angle of deviation experienced by a ray as it passes through the prism, occurring at a specific angle of incidence where the ray passes symmetrically through the prism (i.e., i₁ = i₂ and r₁ = r₂ = A/2).

Part (a)(ii): When light is incident normally on the first refracting face of the prism, the angle of incidence at the first surface is 0°, so the ray enters without bending (r₁ = 0). Inside the prism, the ray travels and hits the second face. Since r₁ + r₂ = A (property of the prism), r₂ = A. At the second face, Snell's law gives n sin r₂ = sin(angle of emergence). The total deviation δ = (angle of incidence at first face – r₁) + (angle of emergence – r₂) = 0 + (angle of emergence – A). So angle of emergence = A + δ. Applying Snell's law at the second face: n sin A = sin(A + δ), giving n = sin(A + δ)/sin A.

Part (a)(iii): Given n = √2, A = 60°. Using the minimum deviation formula n = sin((A + δ_m)/2)/sin(A/2): √2 = sin((60° + δ_m)/2)/sin 30° = sin((60° + δ_m)/2)/0.5. So sin((60° + δ_m)/2) = √2 × 0.5 = 0.7071 = 1/√2, giving (60° + δ_m)/2 = 45°. Therefore δ_m = 90° – 60° = 30°. The angle of minimum deviation is 30°. The angle of incidence at minimum deviation is i = (A + δ_m)/2 = (60° + 30°)/2 = 45°.

Part (b)(i): Huygens' principle states: (1) Every point on a given wavefront acts as a source of fresh secondary wavelets that spread out in all directions with the speed of the wave in that medium. (2) The new wavefront at any later time is the forward envelope (tangent) to all the secondary wavelets at that time. For reflection of a plane wave incident at angle i on a plane mirror: the wavefront AB hits the surface and secondary wavelets spread out. Constructing the wavefront geometrically, the reflected wavefront makes an angle r with the surface. Using the congruence of triangles formed by the incident and reflected rays with the surface normal, it can be shown geometrically that r = i, i.e., angle of reflection equals angle of incidence.

Part (b)(ii): Coherent sources are those that have the same frequency and a constant (or zero) phase difference between them. Two independent sodium lamps cannot act as coherent sources because, although they emit light of nearly the same frequency (the sodium D-line), the atoms in each lamp emit light independently and randomly. The phase difference between the two lamps changes randomly and rapidly (millions of times per second), so their phase relationship is not constant. No sustained interference pattern can be observed from two independent sodium lamps.

Part (b)(iii): In Young's double-slit experiment, the position of the nth bright fringe is proportional to nλ. The condition that the 4th bright fringe of wavelength λ coincides with the 5th bright fringe of wavelength 520 nm is: 4λ = 5 × 520 nm. Therefore λ = (5 × 520)/4 = 2600/4 = 650 nm.
